newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt jails 19 militants for police killings.
newsitem.headline: Egypt jails 19 militants for police killings.

text.p: Egypt's Supreme State Security Court on Monday ratified death sentences for five Moslem militants and sentenced another 19 to jail terms ranging from five years to life for the 1993 killing of policemen and civilians.

Judge Salah Budur gave five of the men life sentences, four were sentenced to 15 years, nine were given 10 years and one man was sentenced to five years in prison. All the jail terms are accompanied by hard labour.
Budur acquitted seven of the men of the charges which included killing 10 policemen and 10 civilians near Abu Tig town, 345 km (215 miles) south of Cairo.

The men are among 32 who went on trial in March for charges that include belonging to the militant al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) and for blasting buildings and shooting at trains in southern Egypt between 1993 to 1994. They were also charged with illegally possessing weapons.
Two of the men sentenced to death are on the run and one of the defendants has died since the attacks took place.
Budur had passed the execution terms last month but they had to be sent to the Grand Mufti, Egypt's highest spiritual adviser, for approval.
